summary: Full-extraction pass over 16 stored Grenada documents: three Ministry of Finance CBI statistics sheets (2018 by quarter, Oct-Dec 2020 and Oct-Dec 2021 by month with annual totals), the budget books (Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure) for 2017, 2018 and 2021-2026, the September 2024 Medium-Term Fiscal Framework, the 2025 Medium-Term Economic and Fiscal Strategy, the May 2025 IMA revenue press release, S.R.O. 12 of 2024 and the 2001 UN General Assembly statement. Added every cell of the statistics sheets (by period, route and money line), the CBI fees / Economic Citizenship revenue lines with their parts and forward years, the 'CBI Committee' dividend line, NTF grants to the capital budget, every NTF-financed capital project line in the 2017-2023 budget books, the 2024 table of NTF-financed projects, IMA expenses, the CBI-linked bondholder payments ('ERI' line), IMA shares of non-tax revenue, the remaining SRO 12 fee terms and one event.

observations.location: p. 1, row 5. Amounts due (calculated)*, 1st Quarter column
observations.notes: Gross amounts calculated from applications approved by Cabinet ('*Is based on applications approved by Cabinet irrespective of the calendar year in which the application was received'), not cash received. category=ntf: NTF donations; budgetary_fees: government (budget) fees on the investment route; approved_projects: investment due to approved CBI real-estate projects. The sheet prints no currency (amounts bare or, on some lines, with '$'); recorded as EC$ like the other Ministry of Finance CBI sheets: the template states 'Figures are quoted in Eastern Caribbean Dollars' (Oct-Dec 2022 sheet) and the amounts match EC$ conversions of the US$ prices (e.g. NTF US$200,000 x 2.7 = EC$540,000 per approval).

events.title: IMA launches a Citizenship by Invitation programme
events.description: The Medium-Term Economic and Fiscal Strategy 2025-2027 says the Investment Migration Agency will develop new migration products, 'including the Citizenship by Invitation program launched in 2025'. No date, terms or numbers are given.
events.quote: develop new migration products, including the Citizenship by Invitation program launched in 2025

gaps: Grenada budget books 2017-2023: the NTF capital-source tables do not add up exactly in three columns (2021 book: approved 2020 lines 120,000 short of the printed total; 2022 book: forward 2024 lines 100,000 short; small rounding elsewhere); recorded as printed, noted on the total rows.
Estimates 2025: Table 3 gives an approved 2024 'Economic Citizenship Programme' of 334.3m while item 18001 gives 280,697,922 for the same year; both kept.
Estimates 2023 Table 6 (2022 sources of external financing) is an image; the NTF row was read by OCR (grant 123.4m), so the quote check cannot match the text layer.

'ERI' in 'International Bonds 2015- 2030 ERI' (Estimates 2025 and 2026) is not spelled out in the books; recorded as CBI-linked bondholder payments because the amounts equal the IMF's 'Bondholder CBI-related payments' and the 2025 book attributes the 2024 interest jump to the CBI bonus payment.

Ministry of Finance CBI statistics sheets print no currency and use a bare '$' on the NTF fee lines; recorded as EC$ like the earlier sheets, although the dataset rule treats a bare '$' as unspecified.

ledger.contains: One-page Ministry of Finance 'CBI Reporting Template: Grenada: Citizenship by Investment Statistics' for 2018, columns 1st-4th quarter and TOTAL: applications received, approved and rejected by Cabinet and number of new citizens, each split NTF / Investment; amounts due calculated from approvals (NTF, investment budgetary fees, approved CBI projects) and their running total; amounts earmarked for general government financing (budget fees, savings for arrears/general financing 1/; the footnote text for 1/ is not printed on this sheet); CBI payments to the Treasury (NTF section 10, CBI section 11, CBI dividends); Treasury CBI account balance; Treasury spending from CBI (capital projects, arrears/other) and its running total. No currency printed (recorded as EC$ as for the other sheets). All cells extracted; running-total cells whose period equals a quarter or the year already recorded (Q1 cumulative = Q1; Q4/TOTAL cumulative = the year) are not repeated; blank cells (e.g. NTF rejections in Q1, 'Grants toward Capital Spending') are not recorded. Checks: parts add up to totals in every column, quarters add up to the year, running totals match the quarters.

One-page Ministry of Finance CBI statistics sheet, columns Oct-20, Nov-20, Dec-20, 4th quarter and 2020 TOTAL: applications received / approved / rejected by Cabinet and new citizens (NTF / Investment); amounts due calculated from approvals (NTF, budgetary fees, approved projects) and their running total; 'CBI Eligible Revenues' (NTF amounts plus NTF fees received, printed with '$'); amounts earmarked for general government financing; CBI payments to the Treasury (NTF section 10, CBI section 11, dividends); Treasury CBI account balance; Treasury spending (capital projects, arrears/other) and its running total. Currency not printed (recorded as EC$ as for the other sheets; the '$' on the NTF fee line is read the same way because those figures add into the unmarked totals). All cells extracted except running-total cells that duplicate the year total, and blank cells. Checks: parts add up to totals, months add up to the quarter, running totals consistent (Oct + Nov + Dec cumulative).

One-page Ministry of Finance CBI statistics sheet, columns Oct-21, Nov-21, Dec-21, 4th quarter and 2021 TOTAL: applications received / approved / rejected and new citizens (NTF / Investment); amounts due and running total; 'CBI Eligible Revenues**' (NTF fees received and NTF; footnote: used in calculating payments on the US & EC 7% bonds due 2030); 'Amounts Due to Government' (budget fees, savings for debt reduction/contingency 40% NTF, grants toward capital spending); Treasury spending (capital projects, debt reduction/contingency financing) and its running total. No Treasury payment or account-balance rows on this sheet. All cells extracted (blank cells and running totals that duplicate the year not repeated). Checks: parts add up; months add up to the quarter except Treasury spending (13,795,953 + 18,855,340 + 25,250,434 = 57,901,727 against a printed 57,901,726, noted).

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2017' (623 pages; ~35 blank divider pages; no table images). In scope and extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (2016 actual provisional, 2016 approved, 2017, forward 2018-2019); the 'CBI Committee' line under dividends (all five columns); NTF grants to the capital budget (Table 6: 22.3m 2016; Table 10: 32.4m 2017); every line of 'Capital Estimates by Source of Funding - 8089 National Transformation Fund (NTF)' (PDF p. 65; 45 project lines plus total, five columns; lines add up to the totals). Narrative mentions (PDF pp. 9-16: NTF grants below target in 2016; Special Projects 6.7m / 5m, Asphalt 5.5m / 5m, Home Improvement 2.2m in 2016) repeat table cells and are covered in notes; the memorandum's 'An amount of $5 million is allocated for 2017' for Home Improvement differs from the table's 6,000,000 (noted on that row). Not recorded: NTF shares of external financing (20.1%, 23.5%), which are ratios to other donors, not programme figures. Out of scope: the rest of the budget (taxes, ministries' spending, general passport and immigration lines, a 'Revised Citizenship and Permanent Residence Legislation' target with no numbers).

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2018' (634 pages; blank divider pages only). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (approved 2017 and forward 2019-2020 added; 2017 provisional and 2018 already in the data); 'CBI Committee' dividend line (five columns; the summary on p. 84 prints '-' where p. 80 prints 0 for 2017, noted); NTF grants (Table 5: 46.8m 2017 estimated outturn; Table 10: 81.1m 2018 budget; text says NTF was 48.8% of external financing while the table says 50.5%, shares not recorded); all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 92; 48 project lines plus total; lines add up to the totals; the 2017 approved total here is 32,480,000 against 32,380,000 in the 2017 book). Narrative on NTF-financed housing programmes (over EC$5.5m spent and over EC$2m disbursed in 2017; 1,300 and 117 beneficiaries) repeats table lines or counts beneficiaries of spending, not the programme; not recorded separately. Rest of the budget out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2021' (635 pages, text throughout). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' forward 2022-2023 (other columns already in the data); 'CBI Committee' line; NTF grants (Table 6: 85.7m 2020; Table 10: 172.1m 2021 budget); all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 90; 97 projects plus total). Column check: project lines sum to 146,072,030 against a printed approved-2020 total of 146,192,030 (120,000 short) and to 85,675,875 against 85,675,873 (rounding); noted on the total rows. Narrative project paragraphs (pp. 42-45): the M-Power 'EC$4.8 million provided for in 2020' differs from the table's 4,000,000 approved (noted on that row); 'Smart Healthcare Facilities - Grenada Phase 2: Total project cost: EC$1 million funded through NTF' (3-year project, no years, not in the NTF table) is recorded with period basis 'unspecified'. Other project paragraphs do not tie amounts to the NTF. Rest of the budget out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimate of Revenue and Expenditure 2022' (605 pages; one table image on p. 17 is the sector table, no CBI content). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (approved 2021 and forward 2023-2024 added); 'CBI Committee' line (all '-'); NTF grants (Table 6: 152.7m 2021; Table 10: 112.4m 2022 budget; table share 49.2% vs text 40.0%, shares not recorded); all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 96; 104 projects plus total). Column check: lines sum to 104,046,000 against a printed forward-2024 total of 104,146,000 (100,000 short) and 152,679,394 vs 152,679,393; noted. Narrative: M-Power 'This project's 2021 allocation was $6.0 million' matches the table; beneficiary counts not recorded (not programme figures). Rest out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2023' (587 pages; summary tables on pp. 6-17 are images, read by OCR: only Table 6 (2022 external financing) has a CBI line, NTF grant 123.4m, recorded with an OCR note; the share cell was unreadable). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (approved 2022 and forward 2024-2025 added) and its three printed sub-lines (Section 10 NTF contributions, Section 11 approved-project government contributions, other fees net; parts add up to the item in every column); 'CBI Committee' line; all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 63; 68 projects plus total, forward years '-'). Para 9 (p. 14) records the change from 2023: NTF receipts and related fees fiscalised as non-tax revenue instead of capital grants (context; already reflected in notes). Rest out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2024' (620 pages). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (approved 2023 and forward 2025-2026 added) and its three sub-lines in all five columns (parts add up); 'CBI Committee' line; Table 11 'Major Capital Projects to be Financed by the National Transformation Fund' (13 projects plus total: estimated NTF funding and allocations 2024-2026; parts add up). The project narrative (p. 25) says EC$23.9m is allocated in 2024 for the Seamoon Cultural Center from NTF receipts against 3.0m in Table 11 (noted). No NTF capital-source section in this book (NTF now revenue). Para 23 (p. 10) on reclassifying NTF from capital grants to non-tax revenue is context. Mentions of overseas missions promoting the CBI programme have no numbers. Rest out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2025-2027' (1,082 pages). Extracted: item 18001 'Economic Citizenship' under head 180 'Investment Migration Agency Revenues' (approved 2024 and forward 2026-2027 added); Table 3 (2024 actual provisional, 2024 approved, 2023 actual) and Table 7 (2025 approved) for the Economic Citizenship Programme and its parts (NTF contributions, approved-project government contributions, other CBI fees); Table 3's approved 2024 total (334.3m) differs from the item's approved 280,697,922 (both kept, noted); IMA share of non-tax revenue 2024 (73.2%); estimated 2025 cost of operating the CBI programme ($40.2m, bare '$', currency unspecified); 'International Bonds 2015-2030 ERI' interest line (CBI-linked bondholder payments; 2024 actual, 2025 budget, 2026-2027 forward); Seamoon Cultural Center NTF financing (EC$23.9m cost, EC$5.0m in 2025). Not recorded: variance percentages; the EC$M summary on p. 89 and head totals on p. 74 repeat the item line; the 2024 interest jump to $122.4m is total interest, not CBI-only; chart-of-accounts pages (pp. 1072-1082) list CBI codes with zeros (account listing, not amounts); '8089 - NTF' source rows are 0.0 throughout (no NTF capital financing). Rest out of scope.

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2026-2028' (1,086 pages). Extracted: item 18001 'Economic Citizenship' (approved 2025 and forward 2027-2028 added); Table 3 (2025 actual provisional, 2025 approved, 2024 actual) and Table 7 (2026 approved) programme parts (parts add up; Table 7 parts 173.9 vs printed 174.0); 2024 actual programme total (553.7m); IMA inflows '4.5 percent of GDP' (2025, wording ambiguous, noted); 'International Bonds 2015-2030 ERI' line (2025 actual provisional, 2025 approved, 2026-2028). Not recorded: variance percentages; chart-of-accounts zero listings; general pay-grade tables (Due Diligence Officer grades are civil-service posts, not IMA figures). Rest out of scope.

Medium-Term Economic and Fiscal Strategy Report 2025-2027 (54 pages; images are charts whose labels are in the text). Extracted: Table 4 'IMA Revenues 2023 and 2024: Old vs New Format' in full (NTF contributions, approved-project government contributions, other IMA fees net/gross, IMA share of non-tax revenue in both formats, IMA expenses 2023-2024; totals already in the data); IMA expenses projections 2025-2027 (Table 12); 2024 interest payments to international bondholders ($78.4m, bare '$', recorded as CBI-linked with notes); event: Citizenship by Invitation programme launched in 2025 (p. 35). Already in the data: IMA revenue 2023/2024 (Tables 3, 4, 6) and the 2024 budget. Not recorded: growth and variance percentages (45.1%, 97.3%), % of GDP columns (no indicator), the AMIGOS Act risk text (event already exists). Rest (macro, BOP, tax) out of scope.

Medium-Term Fiscal Framework 2025-2027 (September 2024, 38 pages; images are charts with labels in the text). Extracted: 2024 budget for IMA revenues (280.7m, Table 5); IMA share of non-tax revenue Jan-Jun 2024 (88%); IMA expenses Jan-Jun 2023 (0.0) and 2024 (37.3m), 2024 estimate (64.6m) and projections 2025-2027 (Table 9). Already in the data: IMA revenues Jan-Jun 2023/2024 and the 2024 estimate. Not recorded: growth/variance percentages (58.5%, 42.0%, 11.0 points) and % of GDP columns. The fiscal-risk text (AMIGOS Act, NTF receipts uncertainty, NTF contingency window) has no new numbers; the AMIGOS event already exists. Rest out of scope.

One-page Ministry of Finance press release 'Performance of IMA Revenues' (May 2025): Jan-Apr 2025 IMA collections exceeded target by $7.7 million; decline from 2024 expected after the 2024 backlog of Russian and Belarusian applications was cleared; 2025 revenues about 12 percent of total government revenue. The 12% and the 2024 context event are already in the data.
ledger.to_do: The '$7.7 million' by which Jan-Apr 2025 IMA collections exceeded target is not recorded: it is a variance against a target (neither the collections nor the target are printed) and no indicator fits. Needs a decision: add an indicator for revenue above/below target, or leave it out and mark complete.

ledger.contains: Grenada Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2024, S.R.O. 12 of 2024 (4 pages, gazetted 26 June 2024, to commence 1 July 2024): replacement Schedule I with NTF amounts (US$235,000 for main applicant and up to 3 dependants; US$25,000/50,000/75,000 per further dependant by type), approved-project minimum US$350,000, shared unit US$270,000 per share (unit at least US$440,000), government contributions for approved projects and significant investments (US$50,000 plus 25,000/50,000/75,000 per dependant), developer fees (application US$10,000, due diligence US$7,500 for developer and each director, administration US$20,000 a year, start-date extension US$10,000). The four main terms and the price-change event were already recorded; the other 15 amounts are added as program terms. Replaced before commencement by S.R.O. 15 of 2024 (same amounts, unit value corrected to US$540,000).

Statement by Grenada's Foreign Minister Elvin Nimrod to the UN General Assembly, 15 November 2001: review of the Economic Citizenship Program to ensure no known terrorists had been granted citizenship, and the decision to suspend the programme indefinitely (event already recorded). Other content (terrorism cooperation, CARICOM tourism programme, economy) is out of scope. No programme numbers.
